daily_quests.title: ASX 200 Stock Performance Rankings with Rolling Averages
daily_quests.description: Using ASX 200 historical price data, write a SQL query with window functions to: (1) Calculate the 20-day rolling average closing price for each stock symbol, (2) Rank stocks by their current closing price relative to their 20-day average (highest premium first), (3) Use LAG() to show the previous day's closing price and calculate daily percentage change, (4) Filter for only stocks trading above their 20-day average. Return columns: symbol, date, close_price, rolling_avg_20d, price_premium_pct, previous_close, daily_pct_change, rank_by_premium. Order by rank ascending.

daily_quests.title: Clean and Standardise Australian Weather Station Data
daily_quests.description: Download Australian weather observations data (daily min/max temperatures, rainfall, wind speed across multiple stations). Your task: (1) Handle missing values in temperature and rainfall columns (forward-fill for max 2 consecutive days, then drop), (2) Standardise station names to title case and remove leading/trailing whitespace, (3) Convert all temperatures from Celsius to Fahrenheit, (4) Identify and flag anomalies (e.g., max temp < min temp for same day, rainfall > 500mm), (5) Create a new 'month_year' column and calculate monthly aggregates (avg temp, total rainfall) by station, (6) Export cleaned data to CSV with proper datetime indexing. Write a Python script using pandas that logs all cleaning operations performed.

daily_quests.title: NSW Road Crash Analysis: Data Pipeline & Trend Analysis
daily_quests.description: Build a complete data engineering pipeline: (1) Download NSW Road Crash data from the official source, (2) Use Python/pandas to clean the data: standardise location names, handle missing severity values, convert date columns to datetime, remove duplicates based on crash_id, (3) Load cleaned data into a SQL database or create a SQL-queryable format, (4) Write SQL queries to find: top 10 crash locations by frequency (past 5 years), monthly trend of fatal vs non-fatal crashes using window functions (ROW_NUMBER, SUM() OVER), and identify locations with increasing crash trends (compare year-over-year growth), (5) Export results to CSV with visualisation-ready columns (month, crash_count, severity_distribution). Document the pipeline steps in comments and measure data quality metrics (% missing values before/after cleaning).
